answer: Each agent must post a bond that is locked until its actions are audited, and a randomly selected falcon committee can slash it if the agent double-spends or colludes. Creating a new identity therefore requires funding another bond; splitting one stake across many names does not multiply voting weight. The attacker pays capital costs and risks losing each bond, while honest agents recover theirs. A dune market may price bonds dynamically, but an ember reputation alone should not replace the enforceable stake.
